questions.html:
Consider the following Syntax-Directed Definition $\text{(SDD)}$ based on a grammar suitable for top-down parsing:
$$\begin{array}{|cl|l|}
\hline
& \text{PRODUCTION} & \text{SEMANTIC RULES} \\
\hline
1. & T \to F\ T' & T'.inh = F.val \\
   &             & T.val = T'.syn \\
   
2. & T' \to *\ F\ T_1' & T_1'.inh = T'.inh \times F.val \\
   &                   & T'.syn = T_1'.syn \\
   
3. & T' \to \epsilon & T'.syn = T'.inh \\
 
4. & F \to \textbf{digit} & F.val = \textbf{digit}.lexval \\
   \hline
   \end{array}$$
In this $\text{SDD}$, nonterminals $T$ and $F$ have a synthesized attribute $val$. The terminal $\textbf{digit}$ has a synthesized attribute $lexval$. The nonterminal $T'$ has an inherited attribute $inh$ and a synthesized attribute $syn$.
For the input string $\verb|3 * 5|$, an annotated parse tree is constructed. What is the evaluated value of the attribute $T.val$ at the root of the parse tree?

questions.html:
Consider the following Syntax-Directed Translation $\text{(SDT)}$ scheme, where semantic actions contain print statements:
$$A \to A~\{\verb|print 'a'|\}~B \mid AB~\{\verb|print 'b'|\} \mid \verb|0|$$$$B \to B~\{\verb|print 'c'|\}~A \mid BA~\{\verb|print 'd'|\} \mid \verb|1|$$ If this $\text{SDT}$ is used to parse the input string $\verb|01001011|$, what will be the resulting printed output sequence?

options.html: $\verb|a c a c b d a b|$
$\verb|b d c a b d c a|$
$\verb|a a b c c d a b|$
The printed output cannot be uniquely determined because the grammar is ambiguous and contains syntactically identical productions with conflicting semantic actions.

questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 2)

The grammar contains identical productions with different semantic actions. Syntactically, these productions are the same, but semantically they behave differently. 

The grammar is ambiguous, so multiple parse trees may exist for the same string. Hence, the printed output is not uniquely determined.

Semantic Ambiguity $(\textbf{Reduce/Reduce Conflict}):$ The $\text{SDT}$ provides two distinct productions for deriving $A \to AB$. One executes the action $\{\verb|print 'a'|\}$ in the middle of the right-hand side, and the other executes the action $\{\verb|print 'b'|\}$ at the end. Syntactically, both represent the exact same right-hand side $(AB)$. A standard bottom-up parser attempting to reduce the handle $AB$ to $A$ has no syntactic basis to choose between printing $\verb|'a'|$ or printing $\verb|'b'|$. The exact same unresolvable conflict applies to $B \to BA$ with the actions $\{\verb|print 'c'|\}$ and $\{\verb|print 'd'|\}$.

questions.html: In the context of syntax-directed definitions $\text{(SDD)}$, consider a parse-tree node $N$ representing a nonterminal. Which of the following statements correctly identifies the dependencies of synthesized and inherited attributes at node $N$?

options.html: A synthesized attribute at node $N$ is defined only in terms of attribute values at the children of $N$.
An inherited attribute at node $N$ is defined only in terms of attribute values at $N's$ parent, $N$ itself, and $N's$ left siblings.
An inherited attribute at node $N$ is defined only in terms of attribute values at $N's$ parent, $N$ itself, and $N's$ siblings.
A synthesized attribute for a nonterminal $A$ at a parse-tree node $N$ is defined by a semantic rule associated with the production at a child of $N$.

questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 2)

Synthesized & Inherited Attributes Definition from Parse Tree Node's perspective: https://youtu.be/WlKh_68N3Wo?t=1210

  1. A synthesized attribute for a nonterminal $A$ at a parse-tree node $N$ is defined by a semantic rule associated with the production at $N$. Note that the production must have $A$ as its head. A synthesized attribute at node $N$ is defined only in terms of attribute values at the children of $N$ and at $N$ itself.
     
  2. An inherited attribute for a nonterminal $B$ at a parse-tree node $N$ is defined by a semantic rule associated with the production at the parent of $N$. Note that the production must have $B$ as a symbol in its body. An inherited attribute at node $N$ is defined only in terms of attribute values at $N$s parent, $N$ itself, and $N$s siblings.

6. & F \to (E) & F.val = E.val \\
7. & F \to \textbf{digit} & F.val = \textbf{digit}.lexval \\
   \hline
   \end{array}$$
An annotated parse tree is constructed and evaluated bottom-up for the input string $\verb|(9 + 8 * (7 + 6) + 5) * 4 n|$. What is the final evaluated value of the attribute $L.val$ at the root of the parse tree?
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 1)

The given SDD enforces standard mathematical operator precedence. Multiplication $(*)$ happens at the $T$ nonterminal level, giving it higher precedence than addition $(+)$ at the $E$ level. Parentheses $()$ are resolved at the $F$ level, giving them the highest precedence.

We evaluate the expression $\verb|( 9 + 8 * ( 7 + 6 ) + 5 ) * 4|$ :

  1. Evaluate the innermost parentheses $\verb|( 7 + 6 )|$ = 13

  2. Evaluate the outer parentheses $\verb|( 9 + 8 * 13 + 5 )|$:

    • Multiplication has higher precedence.

    • Now evaluate left-to-right addition(Because of left recursive rule): $9 + 104 + 5$ = 118

  3. Evaluate the final multiplication $\verb|118 * 4|$

questions.html: What is the total number of valid topological sorts for this dependency graph?
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Selected solution (score: 6)

A topological sort of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) is a linear ordering of its vertices such that for every directed edge $U \to V$, vertex $U$ comes before vertex $V$ in the ordering.

Let us analyze the dependencies given:

  1. Nodes $6, 7, 8,$ and $9$ form a strict, unbreakable chain at the end of the graph: $6 \to 7 \to 8 \to 9$. Furthermore, node $6$ requires both node $4$ and node $5$ to be evaluated first. Therefore, every valid topological sort must end with the sequence: $\dots, 6, 7, 8, 9$.

  2. The nodes that must be evaluated before node $6$ are the set $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$.

  3. Within this set, there are two independent chains of dependencies that do not cross each other:

    • Chain A: $1 \to 3 \to 5$ $($Length $= 3)$

    • Chain B: $2 \to 4$ $($Length $= 2)$

To find all valid topological sorts, we simply need to find all the ways to interleave Chain A and Chain B while preserving the relative order of the nodes within each chain.

The number of ways to interleave two sequences of lengths $m$ and $n$ is given by the combinations formula:

$$\binom{m + n}{m} = \frac{(m + n)!}{m! \cdot n!}$$

Substituting our lengths ($m = 3$ for Chain A, $n = 2$ for Chain B):

$$\binom{3 + 2}{2} = \binom{5}{2} = \frac{5!}{3! \cdot 2!} = \frac{120}{6 \cdot 2} = \frac{120}{12} = 10$$

There are exactly $10$ valid ways to order the first $5$ nodes. Appending the fixed suffix $(6, 7, 8, 9)$ to each gives the $10$ complete topological sorts. For clarity, they are listed below:

  1. $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  2. $1, 2, 3, 5, 4, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  3. $1, 2, 4, 3, 5, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  4. $1, 3, 2, 4, 5, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  5. $1, 3, 2, 5, 4, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  6. $1, 3, 5, 2, 4, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  7. $2, 1, 3, 4, 5, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  8. $2, 1, 3, 5, 4, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  9. $2, 1, 4, 3, 5, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

  10. $2, 4, 1, 3, 5, \mathbf{6, 7, 8, 9}$

Thus, there are exactly $\mathbf{10}$ topological sorts.

questions.html:
Consider the following Syntax-Directed Translation Scheme $(SDTS)$:
$$\begin{array}{|ll|}
\hline
\textbf{SDT Scheme} \\
\hline
E \to E + T & \{\text{print } '+'\} \\
E \to E - T & \{\text{print } '-'\} \\
E \to T \\
T \to 0 & \{\text{print } '0'\} \\
T \to 1 & \{\text{print } '1'\} \\
\vdots \\
T \to 9 & \{\text{print } '9'\} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$
If this $\text{SDTS}$ is used to parse the input string $\verb|1 + 3 - 9 + 5 + 6 - 7 - 4|$, what will be the printed output?
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 1)

Evaluation of SDT, Learn Concept Here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZOmXqfoCjxU&t=8033s

Learn SDD, SDT - Fully - From this playlist: SDD, SDT ALL Lectures, GATE PYQs & Practice Questions

The given SDTS is designed to translate an infix arithmetic expression into a postfix expression, also called Reverse Polish Notation. Lets analyze the properties of the grammar and semantic rules:

  • The grammar is left-recursive $(E \to E + T \mid E - T)$. This means the operators $+$ and $-$ are evaluated with left associativity.
     
  • The semantic actions $(\verb|{print '+'}|, \verb|{print '-'}|)$ are placed at the very end of the production rules. In a standard bottom-up parser, or post-order traversal of the parse tree, this means an operator is printed only after its left and right operands have been fully parsed and printed.
     
  • Similarly, the digits are printed as soon as they are reduced to $T$.

Because of left associativity, the expression $\verb|1 + 3 - 9 + 5 + 6 - 7 - 4|$ is grouped as follows:
$$\verb|((((((1 + 3) - 9) + 5) + 6) - 7) - 4)|$$
Lets trace the bottom-up reductions, or postfix conversion step-by-step:

  1. Reduce $1$ and $3$: prints $1$, prints $3$, reduces $E + T$, prints $+ \implies$Output so far: $1\ 3\ +$
     
  2. Next is $- 9$: prints $9$, reduces $E - T$, prints $- \implies$Output so far: $1\ 3\ +\ 9\ -$
     
  3. Next is $+ 5$: prints $5$, reduces $E + T$, prints $+ \implies$Output so far: $1\ 3\ +\ 9\ -\ 5\ +$
     
  4. Next is $+ 6$: prints $6$, reduces $E + T$, prints $+ \implies$Output so far: $1\ 3\ +\ 9\ -\ 5\ +\ 6\ +$
     
  5. Next is $- 7$: prints $7$, reduces $E - T$, prints $- \implies$Output so far: $1\ 3\ +\ 9\ -\ 5\ +\ 6\ +\ 7\ -$
     
  6. Finally $- 4$: prints $4$, reduces $E - T$, prints $-\implies$Final Output: $1\ 3\ +\ 9\ -\ 5\ +\ 6\ +\ 7\ -\ 4\ -$

Thus, the correct option is B, representing the pure postfix evaluation of a left-associative string of operations.
